newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares open flat, seen staying flat.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares open flat, seen staying flat.

text.p: Shares opened flat in Singapore on Wednesday with a lacklustre day in prospect, dealers said.
"It's times like this I wish I was in another job. It's really boring out there," said one dealer with a local firm.
A slow start to the day saw a meager 31.5 million shares traded in the first 90 minutes of trade, although gainers were ahead of losers 125 to 67.
At 0230 GMT the Straits Times Industrials Index was slightly down, off 3.77 points at 2,057.45.
DBS Land shares dipped Singapore $0.14 to S$4.86 in early trade after Tuesday's placement of 19 million shares at S$4.75.
Dealers said they expected the price to recover once the market absorbed the positive implications of the issue.
Parkway Holdings, the healthcare group in which DBS Land has a 19 percent stake and thought by market sources to be an eventual takeover target, was down five cents at S$6.95.

Recently listed paper and packaging materials firm New Toyo International topped actives in early trade, hitting a high of S$0.905, near the S$0.92 value analysts think the stock should be trading at. At 0230 GMT it settled back to S$0.895.
